scope: Source review of remaining pinned wireless task/timer compatibility; no new runtime fault injection

findings.observation: Task creation allocates the requested byte stack plus 2048 bytes from heap and creates a native semaphore/task; start failure does not free the allocated stack. Task-entry selection is not reserved before leaving its critical section.
findings.consequence: Not a static application task lifecycle; concurrent creation and failure cleanup need review.
findings.remedy: Precreate named, bounded service tasks and notification objects with owned aligned stacks; use checked binding/lifecycle transitions, fixed capacity and no runtime allocation fallback.

findings.observation: Increment/give coalesce into a binary semaphore; without-overwrite has no value/state branch, previous-value outputs are ignored, state/value-clear APIs are stubs, and entry bits clear even with pending notification.
findings.consequence: Some valid SDK notification sequences do not have FreeRTOS semantics. One successful radio operation does not validate other callers.
findings.remedy: Owned fixed per-task notification value and pending/waiting state, atomic transitions, one configured index, independent model/interleaving tests and real ISR/task handoff.

findings.observation: Priority-get returns constant 5; priority-set ignores a null current-task handle and casts T_CTSK storage to T_RTSK; native tasks share fallback TLS and deletion callbacks are ignored.
findings.consequence: Priority and per-task SDK state are not generally preserved. The cast requires a correct native object type, independent of whether current layouts happen to fit.
findings.remedy: Use validated handles and exact native result types, actual priorities and per-task TLS; define retained service shutdown semantics.

findings.observation: Both dynamic and static timer APIs allocate a descriptor and native alarm/cyclic; the static control pointer is ignored. Callbacks execute from native task-independent context. Period changes update metadata without recreating the cyclic period. Expiry accessor is a stub.
findings.consequence: Static-storage, daemon-task callback and period/expiry contracts are incomplete. SDK timer macros and linked symbol reachability also require an ABI audit.
findings.remedy: A permanent timer-service task with bounded command records and precreated wake resources; fixed descriptors, serialized period/deletion transitions and task-context callbacks.

findings.observation: The inspected probe sdkconfig is 1000 Hz, shim header is 1000 Hz and native CNF_TIMER_PERIOD is 1 ms. No current 100-versus-1000 tick mismatch was established.
findings.consequence: Do not diagnose a conversion bug from stale comments or unrelated default configurations.
findings.remedy: Pin/check actual compiled settings; reject unsupported tick configurations before future integration.

findings.observation: Queue/event replacement does not cover SDK radio buffers, NimBLE host/controller, lwIP messages/pbufs, HTTP/MQTT/TLS state or FreeRTOS task/timer paths.
findings.consequence: No whole-system no-malloc or late-object claim follows from the USB core or isolated advertising.
findings.remedy: Inventory actual request counts/bytes and call sites, assign fixed reservations, qualify reconnect/exhaustion/flash-save behavior; justify only any expressly permitted Wi-Fi-driver exception, never blanket BLE/application exemptions.

limits: Line numbers locate inspected implementations; findings are not proof each path is reached in the current diagnostic.
Successful scan/advertising does not close these gaps or qualify association/GATT/coexistence.
No credentials, network association or phone actions were used for this review.
